P1.evidence: P1a miss — nothing from an application or setter notes was read back, and no setter is referenced anywhere on the call. P1b partial, the standard three of four: 'these calls are very simple, I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, where are you trying to get to, and if there's an alignment we can talk about it, if not that's fine too, we just shake hands and part as friends.' What you need was again unframed. P1c hit — 'sounds good' asked and agreed. P1d partial: instead of the scripted open question the rep asked a context question, 'tell me how well do you know Trevor and his work, the kettlebell training?' It functioned well — the answer produced the Ehlers-Danlos disclosure inside forty seconds — but it is a source question, not an invitation to state what they want help with.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch. P2a hit — 'roughly where are you at in terms of your weight and your height?' and 'how old are you?', and when the weight answer came back vague ('technically obese') he returned to it later and got 220 lb. P2b hit — occupation, the seven baseball fields, and crucially whether the work is sedentary: 'You move around a lot?' produced five to ten miles of walking a day, and later the full 3am-to-3.30pm schedule with commute. P2c hit — asked directly: 'apart from those injuries that you mentioned, do you have any like chronic conditions or anything like that?' P2d hit and by a distance the best injury questioning in the batch. He did not stop at the first answer on anything: 'How does that show up with the hips? Is it stiff or what's going on?', then 'what's going on with your lower back? Is it like pain?', then 'what's going on with the knees?', then 'is it like on a daily basis, like you feel it when you walk?' And uniquely in this batch he asked about clinical involvement and compliance: 'did you went to a doctor or like physiotherapist?', 'Did they assign you like with some workout regimen?', 'Did you follow that?', 'Are you doing that still?' — producing 'Should be, but no.' P2e hit — current training, home versus gym, and prior gym history all established. P2f partial — results from current training were not asked as such, though the physiotherapy-adherence line covered adjacent ground. P2g hit — nutrition asked, then 'And vegetables?', then the sweet tooth and alcohol frequency chased down. P2h miss, and it is the most conspicuous miss in the batch: this man wakes at 3am, drives, works a physical job until 2.30pm, drives 30 to 50 minutes home, and said in as many words 'I'm just tired, man.' Sleep quantity and quality were never asked. P2i hit — 'does that in any way affect you on a day-to-day? Like your work, your energy?', which produced the twelve-acre spraying story and the ice packs.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — 'if you would have to say, stated in your own words, what would be your main goal? Let's put it like in six months time, where would you like to be?' and he then quantified it properly, pushing past 'core muscles' to a waist size, a bodyweight and a date last held. P3b partial — the scripted mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered; instead he built his own forced choice between comfort and pain, which worked but is a different move. P3c hit, and it produced the best material on the call: asking what would change if the pain went produced archery, and he then tested it — 'Are you able to do that right now?' — surfacing that he manages about two quivers before his shooting degrades. P3d hit, run several times: 'Why is that more important than not feeling good on the beach?', 'how long have you actually been thinking about changing your situation, your health?', and 'Was there any particular moment that made you make this move? That you thought enough is enough?' P3e hit — 'if you think about what would actually change for you if you actually take care of this... how would you operate differently?' P3f miss — who else this impacts was never asked, and as a result nothing at all is known about whether this prospect has a partner or children. P3g partial — identity and ageing came through strongly ('I feel like I'm probably 10 years older than what I should be, comparative to my friends') and the rep future-paced six to eight months out, but family, marriage and legacy were never touched. P3h hit and textbook: 'from what I'm seeing, it's not only about feeling comfortable on the beach, but it's also about actually going through the day without pain. Would that be accurate?' — answered 'Yes, sir.'

P4.evidence: The third clean sweep of this phase by this rep in four days, and the best executed. P4a hit — 'Have you tried anything, actually, to get in better shape?' P4b hit — the outcomes were elicited in detail: the massage therapist moved away, the chiropractor 'would feel good for about a day, day or so, and then the pain would be back', the physiotherapist's exercises stopped. P4c hit — 'what do you feel like has actually been stopping you from fixing this up to this point?' P4d hit, and this is the standout moment of the call: the prospect gave the standard non-answer, 'Probably motivation, if I'm being honest', and the rep refused it — 'motivation is like, it's an emotion, it comes. It doesn't stick for a longer time. One day you're motivated, another day you're not. So, like, what's been really going on?' That produced the real obstacle: 'I would say motivation, but also, I'm just tired, man. I get up at 3.' P4e hit — the prospect named his own gap unprompted and precisely: 'everybody has the internet, so you have all the opportunity, right, but I lack the understanding and the system to go towards, because there's so many options that you can go with.' P4f hit — the substance of the information-isn't-the-problem move was achieved by that same line, elicited by the rep's persistence rather than handed over.

P5.evidence: The best consequence frame in the batch, and the only one where the rep had to fight for it. P5a hit, verbatim: 'Have you thought about what would it be if actually nothing changes, like in two years, five years, how it's going to be?' P5b hit, and this is the phase working properly under resistance. The prospect minimised — 'It's not going to be terrible if I weren't to change' — and the rep did not accept it. He came back with 'So do you think it's going to be the same or it's going to be worse?', got 'Probably worse', then used the prospect's own evidence against the minimisation: 'You got an issue from just holding a door.' Then he asked a third time: 'let me ask you again, do you really think that it's not going to be that bad in two years, three years, if you're not going to actually do something about it?' The answer changed to 'It won't be good. I'll tell you that much.' Three attempts to move a prospect off a comfortable answer is exactly what this check is for. P5c partial — 'why not' was never asked as a question; the rep asserted it instead ('I can only assume that staying at this current level is not acceptable to you') and got the answer anyway. P5d hit, in the strongest variant anywhere in this batch. Rather than the scripted line-in-the-sand phrasing he ran an ownership sequence: 'whose responsibility actually is it to make a change?' / 'Mine.' / 'Why so?' / 'Because I'm the only one that can help me.' He then pre-framed resistance ('we are masters of self-sabotage'), ran the devil-and-angel exercise to surface the self-sabotaging voice verbatim ('just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts'), had the prospect choose which voice to listen to and say why, and closed with a mandate: 'do I have your permission to hold you accountable, to hold you to the fire?' / 'Yeah.' / 'You sure? Because you know I will.'

P6.evidence: P6a hit, and correctly placed after the pillars and before the number: 'just to make sure we are on the same page, if you had the right training, simple nutrition, and real accountability, all built around your life, would you agree that you would get to your dream physique, and especially that you're going to be pain-free?' — answered 'Yes.' P6b hit and run early, before any presentation, at 00:31:03: 'is there anything outside yourself that would stop you from committing to this fully?' It was then re-run before pricing: 'if we can figure out the details, talk about the numbers, but are you fully actually committed to showing up and doing the work to become the better version of Alex?' — 'Yes.' P6c partial, and this is where the call went wrong, though not in the way the check usually fails. The yes was clear and correctly obtained. The problem is that the answer to P6b contained a warning the rep did not act on: 'Other than I'm curious on the financial side of it. And then, no.' The script's own instruction is to move forward only once you have a clear yes, and this was a conditional one. It was also the third financial signal of the call, after 'money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper' at 00:07:39 and 'a good amount of it right now has been due to my financial instability' at 00:17:09. Three flags, none qualified, and sixteen more minutes of building toward a $6,000 number.

P11.evidence: Both tiers were priced and a recommendation was made, but the prospect refused immediately and absolutely, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome sequence were never reachable. Scored N/A so the phase does not double-penalise a refusal that no execution could have converted.

objection_plays.detail: The textbook run of this play in the batch, and the only one that scores a hit. ISOLATE FIRST ran twice, because the first attempt was deflected: 'just to make sure, finances side, are you, like, you feel confident that you actually can get to your goals with this?' got a restatement of the money problem, so he re-asked more precisely — 'What I'm asking is, are you 100% confident on the program itself, how it's structured, and that you actually can get to your goals?' — and got a clean 'Yes.' The should-versus-how move followed almost verbatim: 'you're not in a, let's say, should place, but, like, how to do it?' — 'Correct.' He confirmed the isolation a third time ('it's just a matter of working out the financials. Am I correct?') and even checked the self-sabotage voice was quiet ('So there's no devil screaming anything right now?'). He opened the payment door, then asked permission in the scripted form: 'are you comfortable having like an open and honest conversation about exactly where you're financially at right now?' Then the financial picture: cash on hand ('What's your cash on hand right now?' — $40), a probe into how that is possible, and credit cards ('do you have any credit cards that you could use?' — 'Could, but I'm paying that off right now'). Monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit and investments were not asked, and scoring this a hit rather than a partial is deliberate: the play's purpose is to establish whether the money can be found, that was established beyond doubt, and continuing to itemise a man with $40 for gas would have been extractive rather than diligent. Stopping was the correct execution.

Triggered by the prospect's own deferral — 'when I get to the financial point that I can do this... once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all.' The rep ran the play's core question, which is the one that matters: 'how do you feel when you said that you're gonna pay that off? Like, what's the timeframe?' The answer was two years for the retirement loan and no defined date for the credit card. None of the pressure moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. Scored partial, and the omission is defensible: the prospect's constraint is arithmetic, not psychology, and applying urgency to it would have been the wrong call. What is worth noting is that the rep had earned the right to use those lines — he had just established, over three attempts, that the joint problems will be worse in two years — and chose not to.

Run pre-emptively and to full effect, before the price, as inoculation rather than rebuttal. The rep pre-framed resistance — 'with anything that we change in life, there is always some level of resistance. We are masters of self-sabotage. Our brains are just basically wired to keep us safe and comfortable' — then asked for the accountability mandate and, when the answer was hedged ('I want to say yes'), pursued it: 'What makes you not saying that?' / 'Myself. Knowing myself.' He then externalised the doubt with the devil-and-angel exercise and got the self-sabotaging script quoted verbatim: 'just another one of these. Let's see how long this one lasts.' He had the prospect identify which voice the future version of himself needs to listen to, commit to it, and say why it was different this time — producing 'tired of feeling, tired of feeling' and 'having somebody that's keeping me accountable is a huge step in the right direction.' That is Objection E used before the objection exists, which is the strongest possible application, and it is the single best-run sequence in this batch.

SCRIPT AND PROCESS GAP — no price pre-frame anywhere upstream. 'I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time.' This prospect came from an Instagram advertisement, did not know who Trevor was ('not at all actually'), and reached minute forty-seven with no idea of the order of magnitude. There is no play for this because it is not a rep problem: it is a qualification and setting problem, and it is the second occurrence in this batch after Jorge Fernández, who arrived saying 'I don't know why I'm on this call.' Both were ad-sourced, both had no money, and both consumed most of an hour of closing time. A budget or price-band question at the setting stage would have caught both.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical fit, and the most physically serious instance in the batch. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is a genetic connective tissue disorder; this prospect partially dislocated a shoulder catching a swinging door and subluxes a kneecap while walking. He is under the care of both a chiropractor and a physical therapist. The rep did better than anyone else in this batch on the front half of this — he is the only one who asked whether clinicians were involved and whether prescribed exercises were being followed — and then never asked the one question that matters: whether either clinician would sanction loaded ballistic kettlebell work for a hypermobility disorder. Instead the training pillar was presented as the answer to exactly those symptoms. The known gap in the playbook covers a clinician ruling the movement library out; here there is no mechanism to even consult one, and the prospect would not have known to ask.

SCRIPT GAP — cost-constrained nutrition. The prospect disclosed at 00:07:39 that he eats more carbohydrate than he wants because it is cheaper, and mentioned that he schedules groceries out. Thirty-two minutes later the nutrition pillar prescribed whole foods, eggs, meat, chicken, vegetables and fruit, with no reference to cost at all. There is no play, and no version of the pillar, for a prospect whose binding nutrition constraint is a grocery budget rather than knowledge or discipline. The rep engaged the sweet tooth by name and left the affordability of the prescription entirely unaddressed.

notes: The best-run call in this batch and a correct loss, which makes it the clearest evidence that process quality and outcome are separable here. Four phases scored hits — the baseline, goals, root cause and, uniquely, the consequence frame — and the commitment check and money play both ran properly and in the right order. Specific things worth extracting for coaching: refusing 'probably motivation' as an answer and getting 'I'm just tired, man, I get up at 3'; asking three times, against resistance, whether the joints will really be fine in two years, and using the prospect's own door incident to break the minimisation; the ownership sequence ending in 'because I'm the only one that can help me'; and the devil-and-angel exercise that had the prospect voice his own quitting script out loud before it could be used on him. The money play is the reference run: isolate, re-isolate when deflected, should-versus-how, permission, then cash and credit — and then stop, because the answer was $40. He also closed better than the situation deserved, refusing the prospect's apology with 'it's not about me, my life won't change if you're gonna buy or not' and sending him away with free materials. The failure is upstream and it is a qualification failure, not an execution one. Three explicit financial warnings were given before the pitch — cheap carbohydrates at 00:07, 'financial instability' at 00:17, and, in direct answer to the go-all-in question at 00:31, 'other than I'm curious on the financial side of it' — and all three were passed over. Fifty minutes of closing time went into a $6,000 presentation for a man with $40 of cash. Escalate two things above the rep: an ad-sourced lead with no price expectation reaching a closer for the second time in this batch, and the absence of any clinical screen on a prospect with a genetic connective tissue disorder who dislocates joints opening doors.
